# Schneider names Baumgardt, Wells as EVPs ahead of July 1 CEO transition

by Ashley Kaster, FOX 11 News

Mon, June 29, 2026 at 10:39 AM

Updated Mon, June 29, 2026 at 4:14 PM

Schneider National in Ashwaubenon \(WLUK\)

GREEN BAY \(WLUK\) -- Schneider is making leadership changes under its new president and CEO\.

As Jim Filter transitions into the role of President and Chief Executive Officer, Schneider National, Inc\., effective July 1, two Executive Vice Presidents will each lead a core portfolio\.

Michael Baumgardt has been named Executive Vice President of Intermodal & Logistics and will report to Filter\.

Steve Wells will join Schneider as Executive Vice President of Truckload, also reporting to Filter\.

On Baumgardt’s team, Angela Prill was promoted to Senior Vice President of Intermodal Operations\.

As previously announced, Mark Rourke, who has served as Schneider President and Chief Executive Officer since 2019, will assume the role of Executive Chairman of the Board of Directors and continue to contribute to Schneider’s strategic direction\.

# Schneider names Baumgardt, Wells as EVPs ahead of July 1 CEO transition

by Ashley Kaster, FOX 11 News

Mon, June 29, 2026 at 10:39 AM

Schneider National in Ashwaubenon \(WLUK\)

GREEN BAY \(WLUK\) -- Schneider is making leadership changes under its new president and CEO\.

As Jim Filter transitions into the role of President and Chief Executive Officer, Schneider National, Inc\., effective July 1, two Executive Vice Presidents will each lead a core portfolio\.

Michael Baumgardt has been named Executive Vice President of Intermodal & Logistics and will report to Filter\.

Steve Wells will join Schneider as Executive Vice President of Truckload, also reporting to Filter\.

On Baumgardt’s team, Angela Prill was promoted to Senior Vice President of Intermodal Operations\.

# Bluesky executives will speak at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Francisco

Bluesky CEO Tony Schneider and COO Rose Van will participate in a session at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 dedicated to the question of whether social networks can enter a new phase of development and what role Bluesky might play in this\. The event is scheduled for October 13–15 at Moscone West in San Francisco, according to TechCrunch\.

Schneider became Bluesky’s permanent CEO after serving as interim CEO since March\. Bluesky founder Jay Graber has transitioned to the role of Chief Innovation Officer\. According to TechCrunch, she explained that the company needed an experienced executive focused on scaling and execution\.

In a statement announcing the appointment, Schneider said the team is at the beginning of a long-term effort to build an open web that reflects the diversity of ways people communicate, interact, and make a living\. Bluesky is banking on an approach in which the next phase of social media may be defined not by a single platform, but by a protocol\.

For more breaking news, follow the UA\.News Telegram channel\.

Rose Wang has been with Bluesky since 2021\. Previously, she led the customer experience division at Forethought AI\. At SXSW London, she highlighted the growing need for direct human interaction amid the abundance of AI-generated content in news feeds\.

According to Van, it is difficult for major platforms like Facebook and Twitter to change their approach due to their large audiences; she also described them as, in effect, AI companies\. TechCrunch notes that Bluesky and other platforms thathave emerged or resumed activity following Twitter’s rebranding to X, are a test of whether social networks based on open protocols can retain communities and compete for market share with larger players\.

# Scientific Games Names Kevin Schneider Interim CEO as Pat McHugh Retires

## Scientific Games Appoints Schneider as Interim CEO Amid Leadership Transition

August 4, 2026

News

## Scientific Games Seeks New CEO as McHugh Plans Departure

Scientific Games has announced its search for a new chief executive officer following the upcoming retirement of its current CEO\. This leadership change comes shortly after the company saw changes in its financial leadership team earlier this year\.

On August 3, Scientific Games revealed that Pat McHugh, who has served as CEO, will retire on September 8 after nearly two decades with the company\. McHugh, a seasoned lottery industry expert with 30 years of experience, joined the company in 2004 and advanced through several roles before becoming CEO in 2022\.

Throughout his tenure, McHugh contributed significantly to expanding the business internationally, enhancing the lottery game portfolio, and strengthening the company’s technology infrastructure\. Following his retirement, he will transition to the role of vice chair to support a smooth leadership handover\.

The board has appointed Kevin Schneider as the interim CEO starting September 8\. Schneider, who joined Scientific Games’ board in 2022 and has served as vice chair since March 2026, brings over 35 years of leadership experience to help guide the company through this interim period\. Concurrently, the company has commenced its search for a permanent CEO\.

## Commitment to Seamless Transition

Pat McHugh expressed optimism for the company’s future and gratitude for the support he received during his leadership\. He emphasized that announcing his retirement promptly allows for an open and thorough search to find the most suitable leader for the company’s next growth phase, ensuring continuity\.

> “Announcing my retirement now allows the Board to conduct an open search for the best leader to guide the company through its next phase of growth while ensuring a smooth leadership transition\. Scientific Games has an experienced leadership team, talented employees and a bright future, and I look forward to seeing it continue serving lotteries around the world\.”  
> Pat McHugh, outgoing CEO, Scientific Games

Kevin Schneider also conveyed his appreciation to the board for their trust and expressed enthusiasm about his role during the interim period\. David Nowak, the company’s chair, acknowledged McHugh’s valuable contributions and extended his best wishes, while affirming his confidence in Schneider’s leadership during this transitional phase\.

# Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider Charts Open Protocol Path as AI Tools Like Attie Reshape Social Feeds

Bluesky has grown far beyond its origins as a Twitter alternative\. The platform now sits at the center of a broader vision for social media, one where users control their data and algorithms across thousands of apps\. Toni Schneider, who stepped into the permanent CEO role after serving as interim leader, laid out that vision in a wide-ranging interview\.

He spoke with The Verge about the AT Protocol, the open standard underneath it all\. Schneider sees Bluesky as the on-ramp\. The real story lives in what he calls the Atmosphere\. Over a thousand interoperable apps already run on the protocol\. Daily active apps have doubled since the start of 2026\. SDK downloads have tripled, hitting about a million a month\.

“The future of social media should serve the public good\.” Schneider’s words carry the weight of his background\. Before Bluesky, he led Automattic, the company behind WordPress\. That experience shapes how he thinks about open systems\. Hand off control\. Let independent builders fill the space\. Watch the city grow block by block\.

Schneider wrote his own post to explain the concept\. In “About the Atmosphere”, he describes a thriving collection of apps and services\. Bluesky represents just one piece\. Your login works across the network\. Identity belongs to the user, not any single platform\. Feeds become customizable layers anyone can shape\. Communities spin up their own spaces\. Blacksky serves Black users\. Eurosky operates as a nonprofit focused on the EU\.

But growth brings challenges\. Moderation cannot scale in a centralized way\. Schneider favors a composable approach\. Labels and rules plug in from any builder\. The core team handles some work\. Contractors and independent groups take on the rest\. Private data features will soon shift more activity into smaller, self-moderated circles\. The public square stays focused on civil conversation\. Sports feeds\. Election updates\. No room for the chaos seen elsewhere\.

Comparisons to X come up often\. Schneider points to fundamental differences\. Bluesky sends traffic outward\. Two million clicks a day flow to publishers and creators\. Links do not get downranked\. The protocol stays open by design\. X, by contrast, feels walled off\. AI-generated slop and extreme content fill many corners\. Schneider wants a broader tent\. Less echo chamber\. More genuine exchange\.

Threads and Mastodon operate on ActivityPub\. That standard focuses on server-to-server federation\. AT Protocol takes a different route\. It centers on personal data servers\. Users own their content and can move it freely\. Bridgy Fed already links the two worlds\. Schneider expects them to coexist\. Different strengths suit different needs\. ActivityPub for tight-knit communities\. AT Protocol for true portability\.

AI enters the picture as an accelerator\. Not for training on user posts\. Bluesky has stated it will not use public data that way\. Instead, AI helps builders move faster\. Enter Attie\. The new tool lets anyone create custom feeds through natural language prompts\. No coding required\. It runs on Anthropic’s Claude model and ties directly into the AT Protocol\.

TechCrunch covered the launch in March\. Jay Graber, who stepped down as CEO to become chief innovation officer, and CTO Paul Frazee introduced Attie at the Atmosphere conference\. Attendees became the first beta testers\. Graber put it simply\. “AI should serve people, not platforms\.” The open protocol gives users that power\.

Schneider described Attie as a standalone product\. It sits apart from the main Bluesky app\. Users describe the feed they want\. The AI assembles it\. Future versions could let people “vibe-code” entire applications\. The $100 million funding round provides years of runway\. Schneider ruled out crypto experiments\. Monetization will likely come through fees, subscriptions, or hosting services\. Think WordPress plugins and managed hosts\. The pie grows when more apps succeed\.

Bluesky itself counts around 43 million to 50 million users, depending on the exact month measured\. The user base skews toward those frustrated with X\. Yet Schneider pushes for broader appeal\. Politics proves the hardest segment\. Sports and cultural events offer easier entry points\. The team stays small\. About 50 people work remotely in groups of six to eight\. Low ego\. High agency\. Focus splits three ways\. The core app\. Developer tools for the Atmosphere\. And an exploration group that experiments with AI\.

Decisions split into reversible and irreversible categories\. Quick experiments fill the first bucket\. Protocol changes that could last decades go into the second\. Schneider applies a 10-year lens\. Get the foundation right\. Then the system runs without constant rework\. He sees parallels to the early web\. Vibrant\. Decentralized\. Full of independent voices\. Email works because protocols connect everyone\. Social media could follow the same path\.

Private spaces will expand soon\. Group chats\. Membership communities\. Custom feeds already number in the tens of thousands\. BookSky\. AstroSky\. Each attracts its audience\. The protocol supports video, games, even health data if builders choose that direction\. Bluesky app itself stays text-first for now\. It embeds other formats as rich cards and funnels discovery\. Traffic flows out\. Engagement follows\.

Trademark moves signal seriousness\. Bluesky now owns the AT Protocol name\. The step protects the standard while encouraging wide adoption\. A grant supports Microcosm, a project creating a full mirror of public data to boost resilience\. Discussions on GitHub explore stronger protections against unauthorized AI scraping\. The robots\.txt file currently allows broad access\. Terms of service may tighten\.

Schneider remains optimistic\. The Atmosphere gains momentum\. Independent teams build in parallel\. One adds photo features\. Another focuses on encrypted messaging through Germ\. Tangled supports social coding\. Standard\.site integrates WordPress and other publishing tools\. The whole structure feels like a city under construction\. Coffee shops\. Bookstores\. Residences\. Each fills a need\.

Yet questions linger\. Can new apps achieve critical mass without a dominant player? TikTok on AT Protocol would need users first\. Bluesky provides the initial audience\. But will creators migrate their audiences fully? Moderation at scale remains unproven\. Private data helps\. Distributed labels help more\. The bet is that an open layer dissolves the tyranny of any single algorithm\.

Revenue talks stay vague for now\. Monetization begins in earnest this year\. Affiliate models tied to traffic make sense\. Hosts compete on service, not by locking users in\. Foundations and nonprofits could secure long-term independence\. No rush toward ads\. The unintended consequences worry Schneider\. Better to grow the entire network first\.

Recent posts on X show continued interest\. Users note Schneider’s permanent role and the emphasis on Bluesky as entry point only\. Over a thousand apps already live on the protocol\. The vision holds\. One login\. Many experiences\. Data in user hands\. AI as builder’s aid rather than platform overlord\.

Schneider’s transition from investor to CEO happened gradually\. The board and team approached him after months as interim\. External permanence mattered for credibility with developers and partners\. Internally, the shift felt natural\. His WordPress track record aligned with the mission\. Hand control to the community\. Bootstrap then step back\. The AT Protocol spec may eventually move to the IETF\. Identity directory already sits with a Swiss nonprofit\.

The result could reshape how people experience online conversation\. Less one app to rule them all\. More a web of connected services\. Custom feeds powered by personal choice or AI assistance\. Communities that set their own rules\. Content that travels without friction\. If the bet pays off, social media stops feeling like rented space and starts resembling owned property\.

Attie hints at that future\. Speak your preferences\. Watch the feed appear\. Iterate without engineers\. The same spirit could apply to entire apps one day\. Builders gain velocity\. Users gain choice\. Platforms lose gatekeeper power\. Schneider and his team appear determined to keep the protocol open enough that no single company can close it again\.

# Can social media start over? Bluesky's CEO and COO deliver their case at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026  \| TechCrunch

The next era of social media might not be defined by a platform — it could be written by a protocol\. That’s the bet Bluesky is making, and at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, two of its leaders steering that bet will make their case in person\.

Toni Schneider became Bluesky’s permanent CEO after leading the company on an interim basis since March\. He’s joined by COO Rose Wang, who has been with the company since 2021, for a Disrupt Stage session on whether social media can start over and where Bluesky fits into that potential reboot\.

For founders building consumer products, the stakes couldn’t be higher\. If social media is entering a new era, it creates opportunities for entirely new products, business models, and communities to emerge\.

This discussion — among many others, as well as a wealth of networking opportunities and front-row access to the Startup Battlefield competition — can be seen only in San Francisco from October 13-15 at Moscone West\. And no matter your role within the startup community, we have a ticket option to match\. Act swiftly before prices rise later this month\!

## Why this moment matters for Bluesky, and the social web

Bluesky, along with many of the scrappy platforms that reemerged or were established in the wake of Twitter’s transformation into X, is in a transitional moment\. As the incumbents have entrenched themselves, Bluesky and similar platforms remain a test of whether networks built upon open protocols can retain communities and potentially claw market share away from competitors\.

To that end, Bluesky’s founding CEO, Jay Graber, recently pivoted toward becoming chief innovation officer, saying Bluesky needed “a seasoned operator focused on scaling and execution\.” Enter Schneider, who took on full-time CEO duties following a four-month interim period\.

“We’re at the very beginning of this story, with a decade of exciting work ahead to build an open web that reflects the full richness of how people connect, communicate, and build livelihoods together,” he wrote in his announcement post\. At Disrupt, we’ll see how the first steps toward that decade are progressing\.

Rose’s perspective, informed by having been with Bluesky since late 2021, along with a past role leading customer experience at Forethought AI, is that a focus on users is a part of that rebuild\.

She asserted at SXSW London earlier this year that there’s an increasing need for human-to-human connection to return after a deluge of AI-filled feeds\. And that shift in user need gives Bluesky an opportunity\. “Facebook and Twitter are huge, and they have tons of users, so for them to turn the shift is really difficult\. Also, they’re basically AI companies at this point,” Rose said\.

# What we heard: Nuggets from Saia, Schneider, TFI, and XPO’s recent earnings calls

While the executives were positive about the direction of travel at Saia, investors chose to produce a double-digit move of their own on July 30\. Shares of Saia \(Ticker: SAIA\) fell 11% to about $350 that day, and they’ve only recovered to about $362 since then\.

*Saia leaders reiterated their 2026 capex forecast of $350 million to $400 million in the company's Q2 earnings release\.*

## Schneider’s set on trailers

The leaders of Schneider National Inc\. have focused their 2026 capital spending plan on lowering the age of their fleet, which comprises more than 14,400 power units, according to the 2026 FleetOwner 500 list of the largest for-hire carriers\. On the company’s July 30 call with analysts, CFO Darrell Campbell said he’s satisfied with the state of Schneider’s fleet of roughly 76,000 trailers—which means it’s time to save a few bucks versus plan\.

“For 2026, we’re revising our net capex guidance to a range of $350 million to $400 million, down from $400 million to $450 million,” Campbell said\. “The reduction from our previous outlook is driven by a lower need for trailing equipment and consistent with our ongoing focus on asset efficiency\. Our areas of investment will continue to support growth across intermodal, especially dray capacity, and in dedicated, particularly in specialty equipment\.”

With its move, Schneider is going in the opposite direction of Old Dominion Freight Line, whose executives late last month said they were ramping up spending to take advantage of some “strategic purchase opportunities” in both real estate and equipment\.

*Schneider’s Q2 earnings report features an operating ratio of 95\.4%, an improvement of 70 basis points from the first quarter\.*

## TFI looks to recover from 3PL pricing slip

Many carrier executives have been talking about needing to raise rates to recover rising insurance, labor, and equipment costs\. On July 27, TFI International Chairman, President, and CEO Alain Bédard told analysts and investors that the need to hike prices in part of the company’s LTL business was because “we probably made a mistake\.”

TFI’s LTL work accounted for 38% of the company’s revenue in the first half of this year\. Bédard said business with small and midsized companies is doing well, as are TFI’s dealings with corporate customers\. The issue of late: Third-party logistics work, where TFI’s boss said his teams were “inundated with volume because, probably, we were the cheapest guy in the country\.”

Not for much longer, however\. Bédard said TFI teams are addressing the issue “as we speak\.”

“Now, does that take three quarters? I don’t think so,” he said\. “We know what the issue is\. We know that the market is still soft to assess, but we’re very, very cheap right now with our rates in some sectors\. So we’re going to be fixing that\.”

*TFI’s Q2 earnings release includes details of operating profits in the company’s truckload jumping 50% from the prior-year period\.*

## XPO gathers momentum

The leaders of XPO see the company gathering steam as the year progresses: Strategy Chief Ali Faghri told analysts on July 30 that revenue per shipment will grow more quickly than previously expected this quarter and next thanks to higher rates making their way through XPO’s customer base\. CEO Mario Harik followed that up by saying those improvements, along with the benefits of technology and efficiency programs, should let XPO post a Q3 operating ratio below 81% where typical seasonality would have that figure by more than 82%\.

“If you look at the volume side, it has tracked well above seasonality here more recently,” Harik said on XPO’s conference call\. “And we’re seeing both our initiative in gaining market share as well as the positivity we’re hearing from our customers translate into more freight on our trucks\.”

How durable do XPO’s executives think their progress is? By one measure, very: Harik told analysts that the company’s share gains, with rate increases to close its gap with premium carriers and a push to grow accessorial revenues, have it on a course to improve its operating ratio to the low 70s\.

“We’re able to onboard more of these customers who value service, value relationships,” Harik said before adding that XPO’s “double-digit pricing opportunity is what would get us there and beyond over the next, call it, five-plus years\.”

*The Q2 report from XPO includes a mention of a company-record damage claims ratio of less than 0\.2%\.*

# Schneider Electric elevates Ratnesh Pandey as Vice President, Marketing in India

New Delhi: Schneider Electric elevated Ratnesh Pandey as Vice President, Marketing, Schneider Electric India, effective August 1, 2026\.

In the new role, Pandey will lead the company's marketing function in India, covering brand strategy, integrated marketing, digital engagement, customer experience and commercial excellence\.

Deepak Sharma, Zone President, Greater India, Managing Director and CEO, Schneider Electric India, said, \"As Schneider Electric continues to advance energy technology for a more digital and sustainable future, marketing plays a critical role in shaping customer value, market leadership and business growth\. Ratnesh brings a strong track record of building brands, driving transformation and translating business strategy into market impact\. His leadership will help strengthen our customer connect and help us Advance Energy Tech across India\.\"

Pandey brings more than 17 years of experience across brand management, digital transformation, strategic marketing and communications, including nearly 12 years within the Schneider Electric ecosystem\.

Before the elevation, he served as Director and Head, Marketing and Communications at Lauritz Knudsen Electrical and Automation, part of the Schneider Electric group in India\.

In that role, he led the migration and launch of the Lauritz Knudsen brand across India, the Middle East and Africa\. His responsibilities also included consumer engagement initiatives, including the brand's association with Mumbai Indians as Principal Partner\.

During his tenure at Schneider Electric, Pandey worked across marketing mandates involving consumer and retail businesses, sustainability, energy management software, buildings, home automation and strategic growth programmes\. His experience covered B2B and B2C marketing, customer and channel engagement and brand transformation\.

Ratnesh Kumar Pandey, Vice President, Marketing, Schneider Electric India, said, \"India's growth story is being driven by electrification, digitalization and sustainability, creating new opportunities for innovation and value creation\. As we advance energy technology to help customers become more efficient, resilient and sustainable, our focus will be on building deeper engagement, stronger market relevance and measurable business outcomes\. I look forward to driving the next phase of growth for Schneider Electric's brand and business in India\.\"

Before joining Schneider Electric, Pandey worked in marketing and brand management roles at HCL Infosystems and Digitas India across the technology, financial services and consumer sectors\.

He also completed executive leadership programmes at HEC Paris and INSEAD\.

# Schneider Electric: Most Sustainable Company for Three Years

Schneider Electric employs a global team of more than 160,000 people across more than 100 countries\.

This recognition aligns with the company’s new sustainability roadmap, Impact 2030, alongside its long-standing sustainability commitments\.

## Schneider takes the top spot

TIME and Statista’s list compiles a ranking of 5,000 of the world’s largest and most influential companies\.

Schneider’s position in the list reflects its commitment to making sustainability an integral part of its business strategy, governance and performance\.

In addition to this ranking, Schneider Electric is the only company to have secured the top position in Corporate Knights’ Global 100 ranking twice, in 2021 and 2025\.

It has been named to the CDP Climate A List for 15 consecutive years\.

Sustainability Magazine also ranked Schneider Electric as number one in its Top 250 Most Sustainable Companies list in 2025\.

Olivier Blum, CEO of Schneider Electric, says: “Being recognised by TIME and Statista for the third year in a row is an honour\.

“As energy becomes increasingly central to growth, competitiveness and progress, the need to use it more intelligently continues to grow\.

“We believe energy intelligence is a key enabler of both efficiency and decarbonisation, helping our customers create lasting value while reducing emissions\.

“That belief has shaped Schneider Electric for many years and continues to guide how we innovate, operate and advance energy technology\.”

## Schneider’s sustainability work

Schneider Electric aims to advance energy technology to power progress for all, leveraging its leadership in efficiency and electrification to deliver impact at scale\.

In the first quarter of 2026, the company reported a reduction of its Scopes 1 and 2 carbon emissions 82\.5% against a 2017 baseline\.

It also reported 47\.5 million MWh of energy saved or electrified for customers in Q1, which reinforces its goal of bringing resilience and efficiency to its clients\.

Esther Finidori, Chief Sustainability Officer at Schneider Electric, says: “As we embark on a new sustainability cycle with both ambition and humility, this third recognition gives us confidence that we are on the right path and a responsibility to go further\.

“Impact 2030 provides the framework to scale our impact and we look forward to accelerating progress quarter after quarter\.”

## What is the Impact 2030 plan?

Impact 2030 is Schneider Electric’s new sustainability roadmap, which is designed around four strategic pillars:

- Electrifying the world
- Reinventing the industry
- Unlocking human potential
- Empowering local communities

Through the roadmap, Schneider tracks its performance each quarter, using measurable indicators of progress\.

The company is aiming towards a 90% reduction in Scopes 1 and 2 carbon emissions and a 25% reduction in Scope 3 emissions by 2030\.

It also plans to fund the training of electrical experts to help bridge the energy technology skills gap\.

Peter Weckesser, Chief Digital Officer at Schneider Electric, writes on LinkedIn: “Being recognised as the World’s Most Sustainable Company by TIME and Statista for the third consecutive year is a tremendous honour for Schneider Electric\.

“What makes this recognition especially meaningful is that it reflects not only what we have achieved, but also the progress we continue to make through our Impact 2030 commitments\.

“Sustainability is no longer a standalone agenda\. It is a business imperative, a competitiveness driver and increasingly, a digital transformation challenge\. The ability to use data, AI, automation and electrification together will define how effectively organisations reduce emissions while creating value\.

“I am proud of our teams, our partners and our customers who are helping turn ambition into measurable impact every day\. The journey continues and we remain focused on scaling digital innovation and sustainability together\.”
